 ‘Only The Bell Will Stop Me’ – Chartpayak And Klarob Clash For Fourth Straight Win At ONE Friday Fights 179 
 Two seasoned Thai strikers, two three-fight winning streaks, and one massive step closer to a life-changing contract. Only one man keeps his run alive on Friday night.
 Chartpayak Saksatoon and Klarob NuiCafeboran collide in the flyweight Muay Thai main event of ONE Friday Fights 179 on Friday, November 20, broadcasting live in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s historic Lumpinee Stadium.
 Both fighters have spent 2026 building serious momentum, and both know exactly what the ultimate prize is. A US$100,000 contract with the world’s largest martial arts organization hangs in the balance, and neither man plans to let a fellow countryman stand in his way.
 Chartpayak Is Never Afraid Of Any Thai
 View this post on Instagram 
 Chartpayak has been one of the most reliable fixtures on ONE Friday Fights since the weekly series launched.
 The 28-year-old Kiatpetch product got off to a blistering start in 2023, rattling off seven straight wins to open his promotional tenure. He now boasts a 72-18 career record and an 11-2 ONE Championship slate featuring five finishes. Riding a three-fight winning streak, he has yet to taste defeat against a fellow Thai inside the promotion.
 That unblemished domestic record heavily shapes his mindset. Facing a compatriot holds no intimidation for him, and he is confident his boxing and full striking arsenal can hold up against anyone in the division — provided he stays sharp.
 Chartpayak told onefc.com:
 “When facing Thai fighters, I’m never afraid. I believe I can get past any of them as long as I don’t get caught carelessly by their weapons. I think I have better punches, and my other weapons aren’t second to anyone. As long as I stay sharp and don’t underestimate them, I’m ready to face any Thai fighter.”
 Photo Credit: ONE Championship 
 He has studied Klarob closely and recognizes a dangerous southpaw capable of doing damage with both kicks and punches. In his estimation, the contest will hinge on who establishes their offense first, making the timing battle the decisive factor.
 Chartpayak also delivered a blunt message to his rival, spelling out the high-stakes reality facing both men.
 He said:
 “Klarob is a southpaw who kicks and punches very well. Against an opponent like him, whoever lands first gets the advantage. The key is to win the timing battle in the ring.
 “To Klarob: this fight is a clash for a four-fight winning streak, and whoever loses has to go back to square one. I’m confident I’ll be the one walking away with the win and moving closer to a ONE contract.”
 View this post on Instagram 
 The 28-year-old’s game plan is refreshingly candid. Aware that defense is not his strongest suit, Chartpayak would much rather march forward and dictate the exchanges than concede ground.
 He firmly believes his conditioning and promotional experience will ultimately tip the scales in his favor.
 The Kiatpetch affiliate added:
 “In this fight, I’d rather march forward than back up because my defense isn’t great. Going all-out and attacking first will give me a much better advantage. I’m confident I’ll win this fight and extend my streak to four straight victories because I’m superior in both physical conditioning and ONE experience.”
 Photo Credit: ONE Championship 
 Klarob Has Found His Rhythm, Ready To Trade Full Force
 Klarob’s ascent has been quieter, yet every bit as steady. The 26-year-old PK Saenchai Muaythaigym standout debuted in 2025 and carries 84 career victories alongside a solid 4-1 ONE record. Matching his opponent, he rides a three-fight winning streak built entirely across 2026.
 That surge in form reflects a clear tactical adjustment. Klarob admits the four-ounce gloves required an adaptation period when he first arrived in August 2025, but he now feels completely at home — and his results back it up. His core strengths, however, remain unchanged.
 Klarob told onefc.com:
 “When I first entered ONE, I hadn’t adjusted very well, but now I’ve found my rhythm and gotten much more comfortable with the small gloves, which shows in my results. My biggest strengths remain my punching power and my relentless, fearless forward pressure.”
 View this post on Instagram 
 Klarob has done his homework on Chartpayak and respects his well-rounded skill set, pointing to his clinch work, range management, and lethal left hand. At the same time, he believes he has spotted a glaring flaw whenever Chartpayak surges forward and leaves himself exposed.
 The PK Saenchai Muaythaigym product said:
 “Chartpayak is a well-rounded fighter — strong in the clinch, effective at range, and armed with a dangerous left hand as his signature weapon, which I have to watch out for closely.
 “I’ve studied him and spotted weaknesses too, especially when he surges forward — he leaves openings that give me chances to counter cleanly. This fight comes down to whoever makes the first mistake.”
 Photo Credit: ONE Championship 
 Those defensive gaps fit neatly into Klarob’s blueprint. The 26-year-old intends to meet fire with fire, hunt for an early stoppage, and capitalize on the wave of momentum he has ridden all year.
 He concluded:
 “I’m ready to trade full force — only the bell will stop me because I want to get an early finish. I’m confident in the power of my strikes, especially riding this momentum; if he takes one cleanly, he could definitely go down. I believe I’ll take my fourth straight win.”
